At 1280x900 I loaded big, typed 1.80, pressed Measure, and loaded small 1.5 s later. From 2.5 s to 11.6 s the status read 'Measuring… 2 s' … 'Measuring… 11 s' (the 'Loaded…' message was overwritten), measureBtn.disabled stayed true and the sheet name read 'small-500.png (1120 × 580 px)'. In loadFile, right after `tool.img = {...}`, add: `tool.run++; clearInterval(tool.tick); $('measureBtn').disabled = false;`. Belt and braces, in measure(): `var img = tool.img;` and as the first line of the callback: `if (run !== tool.run || img !== tool.img) return;`

verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced with v/stale.js at 1280x900. I loaded big-2000.png, typed 1.80 and pressed Measure. After 1 s I filled tH with 2.50 and pressed Tab, all during the worker run. When the run finished, tH read '2.50', the status line was the normal 'Every result is measured from art…' and the table showed 'Mass 195 kg', the 1.80 m result, with no warning. Copy reported 'Copied: 118 lines, ready to paste as a build entry.' and the clipboard held height_m 1.8. The cause: the input/change listeners (app.html:1643-1646) mark only the tool.res already on screen, which during the run is the previous result. The callback then stores a fresh r with r.inputs captured at the button press and no stale flag. Round 1 F8 is recorded as 'refuses after the fields change', and this path still lets the copy through. It is the same failure F8 was meant to prevent: the copied entry is not for the height the user typed (2.50 m), while the page shows that height next to 1.80 m results. I did not separately check the reviewer's no-Tab remark, which is commentary; my second loop failed only because the same file cannot be re-set on an input.
verdicts.better_fix: Count field edits: in the listeners at 1643-1646 add `tool.fieldsVer = (tool.fieldsVer || 0) + 1;` before the existing code. In measure(), capture `var ver = tool.fieldsVer;`. In the callback, after `r.inputs = inputs; tool.res = r; writeResults(r);` add `if (ver !== tool.fieldsVer) { r.stale = true; $('toolStatus').textContent = 'The fields changed while measuring: press Measure to update the results.'; }`. copyResults already refuses stale results.

verdicts.reasoning: Rendered text (v/text.js, v/counts.js). The 'top' band note reads: 'The chart's own figures, drawn from their girths, meet this test sooner: 15 of them, from Arnold Schwarzenegger (about 27) up.' The arms card reads: '…already meet this test: 24 of them, from Arnold Schwarzenegger (about 27) up.' The 45–62 gap reads: 'meet the thighs test sooner: three of them, from Ronnie Coleman (about 39) up', and the thighs card reads '11 of them, from Ronnie Coleman (about 39) up'. From limits.json met_by against the page's scores: arms has 24 figures, 15 of them under 40.71; thighs has 11, 3 of them under 45 and 3 under 46.11. So the counts are arithmetically right, but the same sentence pattern, 'N of them, from X (about Y) up', gives 15 vs 24 and 3 vs 11. The only cue to the different scope is the word 'sooner', and 'from X up' suggests every figure upward. A reader sees what looks like a contradiction, so this is a real labelling defect, but minor, not major: no number is wrong. The 'meet reads as pass' part is weaker. Each card's title states the outcome ('Arms can no longer hang down by the sides'), so 'meets this test' reads naturally as reaching that condition, although 'None of the chart's own figures meets this test' under the face card can be misread. The 'evenly widened soldier' wording is already glossed earlier, in the 'top' band note ('on the median soldier's outline widened at fixed bones'), so that part is not a defect.

verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced with v/limfig.js at 390 (dark) and 1280 (light). All four cards have viewBox 0 0 200 218, skull line y=10 and floor y=210. The figure tops (getBBox) are 10.0, 10.2 and 10.2 for the soldier, arms and thighs, but 39.9 for the face figure. Its width is 2.030 m in limits.json (the others are 1.24 and 1.41 m), so limitFigure (app.html:1333) lowers k from 111.1 to 192/2.03 = 94.6 px/m and draws it 170 units tall. wall() still draws the skull line and the template landmark lines for Hd=200. Screenshot v/limits-1280.png: the face figure's head sits well below the blue skull line, and the chest, waist, crotch and knee lines do not meet its landmarks. That contradicts the key ('Blue line across the wall: the top of the skull. Every figure … drawn to it', app.html:1694) and the method's 'Each template is drawn at 1.80 m'.
verdicts.better_fix: Draw all four cards at one scale that fits the widest figure. In renderLimits, after `cards` is built and before drawing: `var maxW = Math.max.apply(null, cards.map(function (c) { var b = Figure.bounds(c.parts); return b[2] - b[0]; })); Hd = Math.min(200, Math.floor((W - 8) * 1.8 / maxW));`. This gives 170. limitFigure then never takes its shrink branch, so every figure meets the skull line, and widths stay comparable across the cards. Alternatively, keep k = Hd/H and widen only that card's viewBox: `W = Math.max(200, Math.ceil((bb[2] - bb[0]) * Hd / H) + 8)`.

verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced with v/caps.js (fallback mono font; Plex Mono has the same 0.6 em advance, so widths match). At 360, 390 and 414 px every caption ('front · 702 px') wraps onto 2 lines (span height 26 px against a 13 px line), and the spans' boxes touch (gaps 0, 0). Screenshot v/caps-360.png (dpr 3) reads 'FRONT · 702SIDE · 702BACK · 702' over 'PX PX PX'. At 1280 they are single lines 43 px apart. The available width at 360 px is about 226 px for three 14-character captions of about 100 px each, so they cannot fit. The cause is .viewcaps (app.html:329-330): flex with space-around, no gap and wrapping text. A 2,000 px sheet adds a character ('2002 px').

In drawSheet (app.html:1447) drop the unit on narrow screens: `'' + v + (innerWidth < 720 ? ' ' : ' · ') + V[v].heightPx + (innerWidth < 720 ? '' : ' px') + ''`. 'front 2002' is about 66 px at letter-spacing 0, three fit in about 210 px, and the gutter's unit can be stated once ('heights in px'). Or place each caption under its view's centre from V[v].x0/x1, as the gutter labels are placed.
